main_body: Altar: a white and lilac upright panel with a cross (rows 11-23), a thin gold edge, a purple front with a cross (rows 26-34), a gold base strip and a grey stone step (rows 36-46)
top_band: No real top band. Only a gold line (row 24, L=208) over a brown line (row 25, L=110), 2 rows in total, between the white/lilac panel above and the purple front below. The white and lilac rows 11-23 are a vertical face (cloth or reredos panel) with a cross.
evidence: The column scan shows white or lilac rows 11-23, then a 1-row gold line and a 1-row brown line, then purple rows 26-34 with a cross, then a grey step. The only candidate for a horizontal surface is the 2-row gold/brown rim, which is too thin to read as a top. The white and lilac area is a flat face-on panel with a cross, so the whole piece is drawn straight from the front, like the red front-elevation and rim-only guide examples. The front detail (cross, vertical stripes) is painted flat rather than inset.

style.evidence: The candidate has 25 distinct colours and a median of 13 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile for the references. Its 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 23%, against 13% and 0%. The large white cloth area and the lilac and purple panels are flat fills with almost no grain, and each material has only about 3-4 shading steps. The dark edge pixels are not neutral (0%), so the outline is tinted, but the flat fills and thinner shading still look flatter than the Beodeul references.
